article.name: dsh-mneme
article.summary: dsh-mneme (Mneme) is a local-first, cross-session memory plugin for DeepSeek Harness. It stores typed memory records in SQLite with editable Markdown mirrors, automatically summarizes conversations, injects selected memories, and can consolidate them in background dream/sleep passes. The implementation also exposes MCP and standalone interfaces. This review is source-based; no runtime or benchmark results were collected.

architecture.text: The durable store is a local SQLite database. The memories table contains typed records with title, content, tags, importance, forgotten/archive flags, source, content history/hash, optional embedding, epistemic status, event/access timestamps, evidence, and document path. The package README describes ten memory types and ten per-type Markdown mirrors; documents are represented as read-only pointer rows.

The package describes a flow from explicit memory_save and end-of-session summarization into SQLite and Markdown, then retrieval/injection and optional background consolidation. The code keeps memory lifecycle, search, plugin tools, and host adapters in separate store/service/tool modules.

The Markdown mirror is human-readable and editable: edits to entry titles or body text can be merged back with human edits taking precedence. A generation/applied-generation state tracks pending synchronization and permits recovery after interrupted mirror writes. The document mirror is a pointer view and is not a human-edit round-trip channel.

Agent and workspace scope labels are stored on records and are part of the same-title deduplication key. The resolver derives identity from the session agent preset and workspace registry/path; strictScope can filter other explicitly scoped records. Scope enforcement and hard-wall behavior depend on configuration and the available session/workspace identity.

behavior.text: Write paths include model-invoked memory_save, session summarization, imports and document registration. memory_save validates supported types and can merge same-title entries only when type, agent scope, workspace scope and sensitivity match; meaningful merges append the new material and keep content history. Session summarization distills conversation content into memory records and links resulting entries to source session sequence ranges when provenance is recorded.

Update/correction uses memory_update for an ID-targeted patch to title, content, type, tags, importance and optional scope. The service records prior content in content history, and when reflection-failure tracking is enabled it can record the old and corrected values. Scope changes also have a separate audit row. Dream/sleep passes can keep, merge, update, archive, create, supersede or freeze conflicts depending on policy; decision runs retain an input snapshot digest, decisions, outcomes and receipt for review/replay.

Deletion has distinct operations: memory_forget suppresses a row from injection, search and lists while retaining it; memory_archive hides it but supports restore; memory_delete permanently removes the memory row and explicitly clears provenance, mint and pin side rows in a transaction. These source paths do not establish cleanup of external backups or copies made outside the store.

Retrieval combines literal keyword matching, BM25 token recall, optional vector similarity, and optionally entity-linked recall; modes include auto, keyword, vector and hybrid. The service fuses and filters candidates, can deduplicate and rerank, applies scope ranking/filtering where configured, and can record the returned candidate list in recall_runs. Automatic injection is a separate path that selects a bounded subset using relevance/importance, heat and current context.

The local semantic-search design documents local, Ollama and OpenAI-compatible embedding backends; with no usable embedder or on embedding/search failure, code keeps or falls back to keyword retrieval. Optional reranking is also configuration dependent. This is a source-level fallback path, not a verified runtime outcome.

limits.text: This selected review covers the official root and package READMEs and pinned SQLite store, service, tools, scope resolver, summarization, dream-decision, mirror and semantic-search documentation. It did not trace every host integration, database migration, MCP/HTTP authorization path, or the full consolidation scheduler.

LLM-based summarization and consolidation can change or omit details; implementation audit receipts make decisions inspectable but do not demonstrate factual correctness. No runtime behavior, isolation guarantee, deletion completeness, index-recovery behavior, multi-process outcome, or large-corpus performance is established by this source review.

The inspected package README and root README were checked for a published contact email; neither publishes one. The repository has no SECURITY.md at the reviewed revision. No email was inferred from contributor, commit, or profile metadata.
